findings.evidence: `argument-hint: [from-ref] [to-ref]` contains two adjacent YAML flow sequences and is invalid YAML. Under the documented host behavior, the body still loads, but the frontmatter fields are discarded.
findings.fix:
Replace lines 2–3 with valid metadata:
description: Draft Markdown release notes from git history between two refs, defaulting to the last stable version tag through HEAD. Use when preparing a release, asking what changed since a version, or writing a changelog entry. Print only; never edit files, create tags, or push. Not for explaining a single pull request (use explain-pr-changes).
argument-hint: "[from-ref] [to-ref]"

findings.evidence: `Draft release notes for the range $1..$2` uses shell-style argument positions, but the pinned command specification defines zero-based positions: `$0` is the first argument. With arguments `v3.1.0 v3.2.0`, `$1` becomes `v3.2.0` and the missing `$2` remains literal, so the explicit-range branch does not resolve correctly.
findings.fix: Use `$0` for from-ref and `$1` for to-ref throughout the command, including the resolution instructions and Gotchas. Explicitly handle omitted arguments before constructing the range.

findings.evidence: `The strict glob keeps v1.4.0-rc1 out` is false: the final `*` in `v[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*` matches `-rc1`. The default-range branch can therefore select a prerelease tag despite claiming to exclude it.
findings.fix: Filter candidate tag names with an anchored stable-version check such as `^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$` before selecting the nearest reachable eligible tag. Do not treat the glob as a strict version validator; explicitly demonstrate that `v1.4.0-rc1` is rejected.

findings.evidence: `git log --first-parent --format='%h%x09%s' <from>..<to>` reads only merge subjects. A normal subject such as `Merge pull request #230 from org/branch` has no conventional prefix and is consequently sent to Internal by line 58, even when its merge-message body contains a feature title. Breaking footers confined to merged branch commits are also absent from the first-parent footer scan.
findings.fix: Keep first-parent traversal for one entry per merged PR, but read generic merge messages with `git show -s --format=%B <sha>` to recover the PR title before grouping. When breaking metadata is not propagated into the merge message, inspect the relevant merged commits for explicit breaking markers without emitting duplicate PR entries.

findings.evidence: The fallback handles only `If git describe prints No names found`. When matching tags exist but none is reachable, Git can report `No tags can describe ...` instead. The preceding instruction to retry from `HEAD^` also fails when HEAD is a tagged root commit. Neither failure has a defined outcome.
findings.fix: Handle the absence of reachable eligible tags separately from invalid revisions and other Git failures. Check that HEAD has a parent before using HEAD^, define the first-release outcome when no earlier tag exists, and stop with an actionable diagnostic if fetching or a retry fails.

findings.evidence: `run git fetch --tags --unshallow once` contradicts `The command is read-only: print the notes, write nothing.` Fetching writes repository objects, refs, FETCH_HEAD and shallow-history metadata; it is also included in the pre-approved tools.
findings.fix: Remove automatic fetching and `Bash(git fetch:*)` from the command. On insufficient shallow history, stop and ask for a locally available start ref or explain how the user can deepen the checkout separately before rerunning.

findings.evidence: `--first-parent yields one line per merged PR in a merge-commit workflow and one line per squashed commit in a squash workflow` spends context explaining standard Git traversal behavior rather than adding task-specific policy.
findings.fix: Keep the exact log invocation and the specific warning against combining first-parent traversal with --no-merges, but trim the elementary flag explanation.
